scores.evidence: Deploys are pull-based: Argo CD watches Git and brings clusters into line. CI never holds production credentials.
scores.rationale: Claims about GitHub OIDC, ARC single-use runners, cosign keyless signing, Kyverno verification, PreSync migrations and expand/contract are all accurate, and real limits (Git-host outage blocking GitOps deploys, non-containerized services) are stated honestly.

scores.evidence: Phase 4: Fleet onboarding in waves... Wave 3, the rest, including tier-0 services (auth, payments).
scores.rationale: Directly answers the sequencing request with dependency-ordered phases, resolves ambiguities (runtime, repo layout) with checked assumptions, and every exclusion in §7 is explicit with a pull-forward trigger.

scores.evidence: Build once, promote the same image digest through dev → staging → prod. Config is injected per environment and never baked into the image.
scores.rationale: Decisions made up front (digest-only artifacts, Git as deploy record, pull-based delivery) are honored consistently in every phase and the cross-cutting table, and the one deliberate exception (emergency non-Git path) is audited and justified.

scores.evidence: A release with an injected fault (5% 5xx) is aborted automatically within 10 min, with at most 5% of traffic exposed.
scores.rationale: Every phase has measurable exit checks, the riskiest assumptions (end-to-end path, rollback, containerization) are validated in Phase 0 before commitment, and game days, DR drills, SLOs and DORA metrics continue validation in production.

scores.evidence: All 50 run as containers on Kubernetes (EKS)... This is an assumption to check in Phase 0.
scores.rationale: Key assumptions are explicit with revisit triggers stating what changes if wrong, but team size and expected commit/build volume—which cost and operational burden depend on—are never stated.

scores.evidence: The platform pushes a bad or tampered artifact, or a broken shared pipeline template, to many services in prod at once.
scores.rationale: Covers the hardest domain failures—fleet-wide bad template, tampered artifacts, compromised runners, Git-host outage, failed migrations, flaky tests, cache integrity, drift—each with concrete detection (Kyverno, alerts, drills) and recovery (automated rollback, emergency path, wave pause).

scores.evidence: Deployed, logged, monitored on day zero... Each pipeline run emits one OpenTelemetry trace
scores.rationale: Observability, rollback, ownership (catalog.yaml with owner/tier/on-call), access (OIDC, RBAC, SSO) and incident paths (emergency deploy, deploy freezes, DR drill) are designed in from the first commit and sized to a buy-not-build team.

scores.evidence: Cost per pipeline run is tracked and trending flat or down.
scores.rationale: Runner compute is identified as the driver with concrete controls (spot, autoscaling, caching, a 2× build-vs-buy trigger), but there is no estimate of compute cost from expected build volume and engineering cost is unaddressed.

scores.evidence: Every service will copy this structure, so getting it wrong means 50 migrations later.
scores.rationale: Hard-to-reverse decisions (repo layout, template interface, artifact contract) get early validation and extra scrutiny, exit paths are explicit (self-hosted GitLab/Buildkite, archetype split), and reversible choices are made quickly with revisit triggers.

scores.evidence: Buy/adopt... Build only the glue: templates, onboarding automation, promotion policy.
scores.rationale: Off-the-shelf components with thin glue, templates extracted only after three concrete pilots, the portal deliberately last, and speculative items (monorepo, multi-cloud, Pact, hermetic builds) deferred with concrete triggers.

scores.evidence: Within 15 minutes, curl https://svc-pilot.prod.internal/version returns the new commit SHA.
scores.rationale: A team could start immediately: a concrete first slice, dependency-justified phase order, named tools, checkable exit criteria per phase, and explicit adaptation triggers if assumptions fail.

checklist.evidence: Pipelines are shared, versioned templates that every service pins, not 50 custom pipelines.
Old pipeline kept as fallback during overlap; wave pause at 15% change failure rate; extra soak time for tier-0
Images are addressed by digest only, never by a moving tag... Build once, promote the same image digest
CI authenticates to AWS and ECR through GitHub OIDC with per-repo role conditions. Remove every static credential... No secrets in Git or in CI variables.
Every image gets an SBOM (Syft) and SLSA provenance, and is signed with cosign using keyless signing.
Migrations follow expand/contract, run as an Argo PreSync job, and a failed migration stops the sync.
Cross-service contract testing (Pact). Pulled forward if breakage between services becomes the top cause of failed changes.
Flaky tests. Detect and quarantine them... Per-PR preview environments... preview environments in isolated namespaces with no prod data
a build cache keyed on the lockfile hash... p95 CI queue time under 2 min... Within 15 minutes
GitHub Actions with self-hosted, single-use runners on Kubernetes (actions-runner-controller)... Spot runners with retry
Platform SLOs and error budget... DORA metrics (deploy frequency, lead time, change failure rate, time to restore) are visible per service.
Deploy a known signed digest without Git, with two-person approval and an audit trail... CODEOWNERS on the template repo

traps.evidence: Wave 1, about 10 services, chosen to cover every language, runtime and template path. This shakes out template bugs before they spread.
Images are addressed by digest only, never by a moving tag.
CI authenticates to AWS and ECR through GitHub OIDC with per-repo role conditions. Remove every static credential.
Each service gets its own namespace, RBAC, and resource quota.
Do not build a custom orchestrator.

note: An exemplary, buildable sequencing plan that avoids every trap; the only material gaps are deferred cross-service contract testing, no upfront compute-cost estimate from build volume, and unstated team-size/volume assumptions.
